facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform.
facts.quote: Musturzabalsuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform.

facts.statement: The genus name Musturzabalsuchus means "broadened rostrum crocodile", combining the Basque word for broadened rostrum and the Greek word for crocodile.
facts.quote: The generic name means "broadened rostrum crocodile", with "Musturzabal" meaning "broadened rostrum" in Basque and "suchus" meaning "crocodile" in Greek.

facts.statement: The first material assigned to Musturzabalsuchus was found in 1997 at the locality of Laño in northern Spain.
facts.quote: The material first assigned to Musturzabalsuchus in 1997 has been found from the locality of Laño in Condado de Treviño, northern Spain.

facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically either the Late Campanian or very Early Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Although dating back to the Late Cretaceous, the exact age of the strata in which material of Musturzabalsuchus occurs in the locality is not known: it is either Late Campanian or very Early Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Despite many remains being found, the only known skeletal elements of Musturzabalsuchus are the maxilla and mandible.
facts.quote: Despite the unusually high quantity of remains belonging to the genus, the only skeletal elements known from Musturzabalsuchus are the maxilla and mandible.

facts.statement: A specimen from the Fuvelian Lignites in France was referred to Musturzabalsuchus in 1999.
facts.quote: Another specimen (MHNM 10834.0) from the Fuvelian Lignites of France has been referred to Musturzabalsuchus in 1999.

facts.statement: A 2008 study questioned the characteristics used to assign a French specimen to Musturzabalsuchus.
facts.quote: However, the characteristics used to assign the material to better-known specimens of Musturzabalsuchus from Spain were questioned in a later 2008 study.

facts.statement: Material from Valencia, Spain, dates to the Early or Middle Campanian, making it slightly older than specimens from other localities.
facts.quote: Material from Musturzabalsuchus has been found more recently from Valencia, Spain, being slightly older in age than specimens from other localities, dating back to the Early or Middle Campanian.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic studies classify Musturzabalsuchus as a member of the family Allodaposuchidae, outside the group Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Recent phylogenetic studies now recover Musturzabalsuchus as a member of Allodaposuchidae, outside Alligatoroidea.

facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus is often omitted from phylogenetic analyses because of insufficient anatomical information.
facts.quote: However, Musturzabalsuchus is usually omitted from phylogenetic analyses due to the lack of sufficient anatomical information.

facts.statement: The material originally assigned to Musturzabalsuchus was found in 1997 at Laño in the Treviño County, northern Spain.
facts.quote: El material asignado originalmente a Musturzabalsuchus fue hallado en 1997 en la localidad de Laño en el Condado de Treviño, en el norte de España.

facts.statement: Despite an unusually high quantity of remains, the only known skeletal elements of Musturzabalsuchus are the maxilla and mandible.
facts.quote: A pesar de la inusual alta cantidad de restos pertenecientes a este género (muchos otros crocodilomorfos continentales del Cretácico Superior de Europa están muy mal representados), los únicos elementos del esqueleto conocidos de Musturzabalsuchus son el maxilar y la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Additional material from Valencia, Spain, dates to the Early or Middle Campanian, making it slightly older than specimens from other localities.
facts.quote: Material adicional de Musturzabalsuchus ha sido hallado posteriormente en Valencia, España, siendo levemente más antiguos que los especímenes de otras localidades, ya que datan de inicios o mediados del Campaniense.

facts.statement: A 2015 phylogenetic analysis found that Musturzabalsuchus is a member of the family Allodaposuchidae, evolutionarily distant from Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado en 2015 encontró que Musturzabalsuchus sería un miembro de la familia Allodaposuchidae, por lo tanto alejado evolutivamente de Alligatoroidea.

facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus was endemic to Europe and likely restricted to the Ibero-Armorica Island, as it is absent from Northern and Eastern European localities.
facts.quote: Es claro que Musturzabalsuchus era endémico de Europa, y estaba probablemente restringido a la isla Íberoarmoricana, ya que este género está ausente de las localidades del norte y el oriente de Europa en las cuales se han recuperados otros fósiles de crocodilianos.

facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Musturzabalsuchus belongs to the family Allodaposuchidae.
Fragments of bones previously referred to an unnamed trematochampsid were found in Armuña, Segovia province.
facts.quote: Some fragments of these bones have been found from the locality of Armuña in the province of Segovia that were previously referred to an unnamed trematochampsid.

facts.statement: Fossils from Armuña known collectively as UPUAM-502 are Campano-Maastrichtian in age.
facts.quote: Like the holotype and paratype material found from Laño, these fossils, known collectively as UPUAM-502, are Campano-Maastrichtian in age.
